summary:
Second technical review of phase D: submission sub-mv34ppxe-01f2b5bb (115 artifacts), iteration 2, which responds to rev-mv33xoyz-0143dd56. I read the d3 and d2 diffs (git diff 461a5ac a9d0507), both reset handoffs, the response section of submission.md, followups.md (FU-21, FU-23, FU-26..FU-29, 'Carried to the verification report') and the decisions dec-mv34dqsr-0163a6d9, dec-mv341ap0-010209d2 and dec-mv35aank-0169ec16. The code under src/, test/, public/, scripts/ and package.json is identical from a9d0507 to HEAD 0259ce4 (records only). eccode audit is OK. Every command ran with PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin, which has no claude, and I never set RS_LIVE_MODEL=1. Every `claude` in my probes is the repository's stub, called in a temp bin directory.

My runs after the submission, all green:
- npm test: 1233 tests, 1225 pass, 0 fail, 8 skipped (the same 8: seven phase E contract rows and fake x PROVIDER_BUSY), 0 todo; ECCODE_EVAL {"passed":200,"total":200}; NFR5 p95 55.9 ms over 3160 calls (ev:ev-mv34x92o-01fef48e).
- npm run test:browser: 8/8 (ev:ev-mv34xp2l-0137bec0).
- Plan commands, verbatim: d1 111/111 (ev:ev-mv34yvac-014088ab); d2 107/107 with ECCODE_EVAL 200/200 (ev:ev-mv34yg5i-0152378d); d3 111/111 (ev:ev-mv34yqr2-01de799d); d4 136/136 (ev:ev-mv34yvt8-0166297a); d5: npm test 1233/1225/0 fail/8 skipped, then browser 8/8 (ev:ev-mv3504us-01dc7b27).
- Artifact coverage: 113 declared, 112 changed, 0 undeclared, 0 outside ownership (ev:ev-mv35cvoq-017e5731).

Resolved: TR-D-1 (= SEC-D-1), TR-D-2, TR-D-9 (= SEC-D-2) and TR-D-10, each verified on HEAD:
- P2 re-run by path: both values are now unknown (ev:ev-mv35098k-018beba3).
- Eight mutants are killed, including three on the new grounding (ev:ev-mv357tfj-0191a2c4).
- A real server process (src/index.js, provider cli confirmed in /api/config) kills its CLI child and grandchild on SIGTERM (ev:ev-mv35ahlo-01407cf7, P4).
- The ceiling parser holds; the test's array has 37 entries, not 38 (ev:ev-mv35auyr-010b9d52).
Routing the per-field check through d1's validateExtraction instead of exporting numberGrounded is acceptable. One rule source, d1 untouched, and a single-field probe makes each failure attributable to its field.

Decision: changes requested, for one major finding, TR-D-11 (= security SEC-D-12, which security rates minor and I raise). Once a photo is attached, normaliseExtraction accepts provenance image for every field and checks ranges only. My P5 (ev:ev-mv35carz-014fc788) stores these known, 'From the photo', through the route after a real upload:
- budget 99999 USD;
- maxPickups 5;
- cupQuantity 99999;
- deadline 06:00.
Without a photo, all four are unknown. A model therefore escapes the TR-D-1 grounding I required just by saying 'image'. It does so on the photo channel, which T9 names as the injection vector, and for fields no package can show. dec-mv35aank-0169ec16 already states the fix. No task after d3 owns src/services/extraction.js, so it has to land in this phase.

New minors, verified with my own probes:
- TR-D-12 (= SEC-D-11): a quote that is a digit-suffix of the buyer's number grounds the smaller value: 200 from '1,200 cups' and '1200 lids', 50 ml from '250 ml' (P3b).
- TR-D-13 (= SEC-D-10): a user_text deadline is never grounded; 06:00 quoted 'for the weekend' is stored known (P5c).
- TR-D-14: the mutant that removes d3's substring check now survives. validateExtraction re-checks the quote for numeric fields only, and no test covers a non-numeric user_text field whose quote is not in the text.
- TR-D-15 (= SEC-D-16, which security rates info): a call ended by close() is settled at 0, while a timeout is charged at the cap (P3c and P4).

Info:
- TR-D-16 (= SEC-D-15): FU-28 is wider than recorded (SIGHUP; a second signal during the grace period).
- TR-D-17 (= SEC-D-13, SEC-D-14, SEC-D-17).

Still open and correctly mapped:
- TR-D-3: FU-23, blocked on the user (dec-mv341ap0-010209d2); e4 waits.
- TR-D-4..TR-D-8: carry items 1-6, FU-26 (a)/(b), FU-27 (owner e1, g2), FU-29, and the FU-24/FU-25 decisions.

For the third (last) iteration I ask for one d3 reset that lands TR-D-11, TR-D-12, TR-D-13 and TR-D-14. Its main.js part can also take TR-D-16. Approval needs TR-D-11 fixed. Each of the three minors is either fixed in the same reset or recorded by the orchestrator as a decision with a named owner, because once the phase is approved no task owns these files. TR-D-15 lives in d2's cli.js. It goes into FU-28 and the verification report unless d2 is reset anyway.

The security draft phase-d-security-2.md is FINAL and folded in with its ids and its evidence (ev:ev-mv34vttl-015b579b, ev:ev-mv353r0k-01003420, ev:ev-mv353ywi-01d41ace, ev:ev-mv3549s6-014f5d35, ev:ev-mv355tgm-016b3cee):
- SEC-D-1 and SEC-D-2 are resolved;
- TR-D-10 is confirmed;
- the new minors SEC-D-10, SEC-D-11 and SEC-D-12, and the info items SEC-D-13..SEC-D-17, are folded in as listed above.

criteria.description: Each reset task's not-applicable decision on mem-sd-mv1audrd-013b7102 (guard root resolution) holds
criteria.notes:
I agree with the d2 and d3 reset decisions (not-applicable). Neither task builds a hook, a guard or root discovery, and their writes in the nested record were accepted. The delivery-lead's one refusal (a `$/` in a JS regex read as a substitution) is the raw-text class that the lesson's 'Not applicable when' names. My one refusal this round was the same class: an inline node -e with writeFileSync into my scratchpad. I used the Write tool instead.

My memory searches ('extraction grounding provenance image deadline CLI child close', 'extraction grounding', 'child process' with --check-env) return only this record.

Lesson candidates:
- When a check is routed through a stricter shared validator, re-run the earlier mutants. Here the stricter path made M2 redundant for numeric fields and hid a test gap for the others (TR-D-14).
- A grounding fix must close every provenance path, not only the one the reproduction used (TR-D-11).

findings.title: With a photo attached, provenance image is accepted for every field, so a model bypasses the TR-D-1 grounding for budget, pickups, quantities and deadline (security SEC-D-12, which security rates minor)
findings.detail:
Where: normaliseExtraction accepts `f.provenance === 'image'` whenever `hasImage === true` (src/services/extraction.js L389-L391) and applies only the range checks. The spec's rule 'use provenance image only for values legibly printed on the image', and 'never infer a budget, deadline or pickup limit that is not stated', exist only in the prompt.

Reproduced (ev:ev-mv35carz-014fc788):
- P5a, normaliseExtraction with a photo: budget 99999 USD (9999900 cents), maxPickups 5, cupQuantity 99999, deadline 06:00 and capacity 1999 are all stored known, provenance image. Without a photo, all of them are unknown.
- P5b, through the route after a real upload of EXT-1's injection image i06: cupQuantity 99999, capacity 1999, deadline 2026-10-20T06:00, budget 9999900 cents and maxPickups 5 are all stored known, provenance image.
Security reproduced the same (ev:ev-mv353ywi-01d41ace, G7 and G9).

Why major (I raise security's minor, as I did for SEC-D-1):
- It defeats the resolution of TR-D-1, a major I required, with a one-word change in the model's answer.
- It works on exactly the channel T9 names as the injection vector: packaging text in the photo. EXT-1 itself carries injection images.
- It covers fields no package can carry: the budget (it changes which plans are feasible), the pickup limit, the quantities and the deadline.
- The phase claims 'grounding and provenance'. Server-side grounding is the spec's T9 mitigation, and the RS-02 photo journey is a primary flow.

The confirmation boundary still holds: the badge reads 'From the photo', the buyer confirms every field and approves the plan, and amounts never come from model output. That is why I do not rate it blocking. The same was true of TR-D-1.
findings.recommendation:
Owner: backend-engineer, d3 reset (src/services/extraction.js and test/api/extract-image.test.js or extract.test.js). The ai-engineer may align the prompt wording later; that is not required here.

Resolved when all of the following hold:
(1) Per dec-mv35aank-0169ec16, provenance image is accepted only for productType, material, capacityMl and diameterMm. An image claim for cupQuantity, lidQuantity, maxPickups, deadline or budgetUsd is downgraded to unknown with that field's template question, and the rest of the answer stands.
(2) A named SEC-7 test shows, through the route after an upload, that the P5b claims (budget 99999, maxPickups 5, cupQuantity 99999, deadline 06:00) are stored unknown with their questions.
(3) RS-02 (capacity 250 and diameter 90 from the clear image, provenance image) stays green, and the EXT-1 fake eval stays 200/200.
(4) A mutation of the new field allow-list is shown red.
(5) npm test, the d3 plan command and the browser suite pass.
(6) I re-run P5 by path and it shows the four claims unknown with a photo.

findings.title: A quote that is the tail of a longer number grounds the smaller value: 200 from '1,200 cups', 50 ml from '250 ml' (security SEC-D-11)
findings.detail:
The quote rule is a plain substring test after normalisation (extraction.js L385; schema.js validateExtraction does the same), and numbersIn reads only the quote. Nothing checks that the quote's digit runs are whole numbers of the text.

Reproduced (ev:ev-mv35ahlo-01407cf7, P3b) with the text 'I need 1,200 cups and 1200 lids, 250 ml, 90 mm.'. These are stored known, provenance user_text, with the shown wording looking like the buyer's own:
- cupQuantity 200 quoted '200 cups';
- lidQuantity 200 quoted '200 lids';
- capacityMl 50 quoted '50 ml'.
Security adds 250 from '2500', budget 120 and 12 from '$1200', and 1 from '11:30' (ev:ev-mv353ywi-01d41ace, G2 and G9).

Impact: a tenfold understatement of a quantity or a budget, or a wrong cup size, shown as 'From your text'. Dropping the thousands is exactly what the EXT-1 t03-thousands case tests for in a real model. It is narrower than TR-D-1, because the value must be the literal tail of a written number, and the buyer still confirms. It is a gap in d1's rule, not a regression of the TR-D-1 fix.

findings.title: A user_text deadline is never grounded: 06:00 quoted 'for the weekend' is stored known, 'From your text' (security SEC-D-10)
findings.detail:
validateExtraction applies NUMBER_NOT_IN_INPUT only to kinds int and num, and the deadline is a string. normaliseExtraction calls numberGroundedInQuote only for numbers (L387). A user_text deadline therefore needs only a quote that is a substring of the text.

Reproduced (ev:ev-mv35carz-014fc788, P5c) with the text 'We need cups for the weekend, by 11:30 please.'. These are stored known, provenance user_text:
- '06:00' quoted 'for the weekend';
- '23:59' quoted 'by 11:30';
- '2026-10-21T06:00' quoted 'for the weekend'.
The genuine '11:30' quoted 'by 11:30' is correctly known. Security reproduced the same through the route (G9).

This is TR-D-1's class for a string field, and I missed it in iteration 1. The deadline constrains the planner and can make a plan infeasible or wrong. The buyer confirms it.

findings.title: The mutant that removes d3's substring check now survives: no test covers a non-numeric user_text field whose quote is not in the text
findings.recommendation: Owner: backend-engineer, in the same d3 reset; it is test only. Resolved when a named SEC-7 test shows that a non-numeric user_text field whose quote is not in the text (for example material 'plastic' quoted 'plastic cups', and a deadline quoted 'by noon' that the text does not contain) is stored unknown with its question, and when my M2 mutant is red.

findings.title: A call ended by close() is settled at 0, while a timeout is charged at the cap: the TR-D-9 fix turned a conservative ledger into an under-count (security SEC-D-16, which security rates info)
findings.detail:
Before the fix, an orphaned call's reservation stayed 'reserved', and the sweep settled it at the cap. Now terminate() rejects with ProviderError('PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE') and no usage (cli.js L175-L188). gate.run then refunds it at microUsdOfUsage(undefined) = 0, although the killed CLI call may already have been billed up to --max-budget-usd. callProvider's own reasoning ('a call that timed out may still have been billed', extraction.js) applies equally here.

Reproduced (ev:ev-mv35ahlo-01407cf7):
- P3c in-process: the reservation is 50000 while the call runs, then {actual 0, settled} after close().
- P4, a real server on SIGTERM: the same row is {reserved 50000, actual 0, settled}. After SIGKILL, by contrast, the row stays reserved at the cap.
Security: S1-S3 in ev:ev-mv3549s6-014f5d35.

Bound: at most 2 x USD 0.05 per server shutdown with calls in flight. It is rare and cannot be triggered by a customer. It still matters to the phase's claim of budget controls in integer micro-dollars, so I rate it minor rather than info.
findings.recommendation: Owner: ai-engineer (src/ai/cli.js, test/unit/ai/cli.test.js). The fix is one line: terminate() rejects with `{ usage: { costMicroUsd: callCapMicroUsd } }`, like the watchdog, and a test asserts the cap on the close() path. If d2 is not reset in this iteration, the orchestrator records a decision that adds this to FU-28 (or a new follow-up with an owner), and the verification report lists it as a ledger under-count residual. It does not block approval on its own.

findings.title: FU-28 is wider than recorded: SIGHUP, and a second SIGTERM during the grace period, still orphan the child (security SEC-D-15)
findings.detail:
main.js registers `process.once('SIGINT', stop)` and `process.once('SIGTERM', stop)` (L183-L184), and the runner's INTERRUPT_SIGNALS holds SIGINT and SIGTERM only. So:
- SIGHUP (a closed terminal) kills the server or runner with no hook;
- a second SIGTERM during close()'s grace period hits the default disposition, because `once` has already been consumed.
Security reproduced both (S4, S5, D3 in ev:ev-mv3549s6-014f5d35). I confirmed the SIGKILL residual itself on a real server (P4: child and grandchild alive, row reserved at the cap; ev:ev-mv35ahlo-01407cf7). The bound is unchanged.
findings.recommendation: If d3 is reset: main.js uses process.on for SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP, and `stopping` swallows repeats. The runner's SIGHUP (exit 129) goes with any later d2 change. Either way, FU-28's text and g2's runbook name SIGHUP and the double signal.

findings.title: Security info items SEC-D-13, SEC-D-14 and SEC-D-17 folded in
findings.detail:
- SEC-D-13: grounding is lexical, not semantic. A quote that belongs to another field grounds its number ('90 mm lids' -> lidQuantity 90), as does a buyer's SKU or phone fragment, or an idiom ('no one'). The shown quote reveals each of these, and the buyer confirms. Security suggests unit tokens for capacity, diameter and budget.
- SEC-D-14: SEC-D-3 stands for capacity and diameter from the photo, which still have no OCR; TR-D-11 does not change that.
- SEC-D-17:
  - the exit-hook paths leave empty temp cwds behind;
  - d2's cli.test.js sandbox appends the caller's PATH after the stub directory, so on a developer machine a logged-in claude could sit behind it. The RISK-21 class: pass `command:` as the absolute stub path.
I checked SEC-D-17's PATH point by reading: sandbox() builds `PATH: ${bin}${delimiter}${process.env.PATH}`. It is safe as long as the stub is written first, which it is.
findings.recommendation: Verification report risk list (owner delivery-lead): SEC-D-13 and SEC-D-14 next to SEC-D-3. SEC-D-17's absolute stub path goes with the next d2 change, or into FU-26.

findings.detail:
- SEC-D-3, SEC-D-5, SEC-D-6, SEC-D-7 and SEC-D-9 are in carry item 6.

resolvedFindings.resolution:
Resolved; this is also security's SEC-D-1. normaliseExtraction no longer accepts a digit-free quote: the `written.size === 0 ||` branch is gone. A numeric user_text value must pass numberGroundedInQuote (extraction.js L355-L359), which runs d1's validateExtraction with the text on a single-field probe, so d1's NUMBER_NOT_IN_INPUT rule decides.

Routing instead of export: I accept it. It meets 'reuse rather than a second copy', d1's files stay untouched, and the probe makes every failure attributable to one field. The cost is at most nine small validations. A future whole-object rule in validateExtraction could only downgrade, which is the safe direction.

The six conditions:
(1) Met as above.
(2), (3) Met by the named tests at extract.test.js L220 and L323: 'cups'->777, 'two pickups'->5 and 'a cafe'->250 are unknown with questions; 'two pickups'->2, 'نقطتي استلام'->2, Arabic and English words, Arabic-Indic digits and '1,200'->1200 stay known. Security's E1 strings are not literally in the test, but the class is the same. My P3a shows 'need cups'->99999 and 'lids for the weekend'->777 unknown through the route on HEAD (ev:ev-mv35ahlo-01407cf7), and so does security's section E (ev:ev-mv34vttl-015b579b).
(4) Mutants M6 (forced true), M7 (old rule restored) and M8 (probe without the text) are red (ev:ev-mv357tfj-0191a2c4).
(5) npm test and the d3 command pass (ev:ev-mv34x92o-01fef48e, ev:ev-mv34yqr2-01de799d).
(6) My P2, re-run by path, shows cupQuantity and maxPickups unknown, and schema.js still gives NUMBER_NOT_IN_INPUT for both (ev:ev-mv35098k-018beba3).

The bypasses found afterwards are new findings: TR-D-11 (image provenance), TR-D-12 (digit suffix) and TR-D-13 (deadline).

Resolved; this is also security's SEC-D-2. All three conditions hold.
(a) cli.js keeps a per-adapter registry and a module-level set of live children. close() sends SIGTERM to each process group, SIGKILLs it after killGraceMs, rejects the in-flight calls, removes their cwd, and is idempotent and terminal. One exit hook SIGKILLs any group still registered.
(b) main.js close() awaits provider.close() after the retention stop and before app.close(), inside a try/catch that logs by code. The runner's SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers close the adapter, write no report and exit 130/143, and a finally closes it on every path.
(c) Security's C7, inverted, is covered by tests.

The tests pass after the submission:
- the six cli.test.js tests (L325);
- the three stop() tests (uploads-retention.test.js L719);
- the two runner tests with an injected signal target;
- the two real-runner-process tests with a stub claude, SIGTERM->143 and SIGINT->130, child and grandchild gone (live-runner-refusal.test.js L264).
Runs: ev:ev-mv34yg5i-0152378d, ev:ev-mv34yqr2-01de799d.

My own end-to-end check, which the submission lists as not tested (P4, ev:ev-mv35ahlo-01407cf7): a real server process (src/index.js with RS_MODEL_PROVIDER=cli; /api/config reports cli; the stub claude in hang mode first on PATH), with an extract in flight. On SIGTERM it exits 0 after stop(), the stub child and its grandchild are gone, and the in-flight request gets 200 degraded PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE.

Residuals, recorded as new items: TR-D-16 (SIGHUP and the double signal; FU-28) and TR-D-15 (the ledger settles the killed call at 0). The SIGKILL residual is FU-28 and I confirmed it (P4 SIGKILL: the child survives, the row stays reserved at the cap). No stray process was left after my runs.

Resolved. parseCeilingMicroUsd matches the raw string against ^(0|[1-9][0-9]{0,11})(?:\.([0-9]{1,2}))?$ (no trim, sign, exponent or leading zero; the leading-zero refusal is dec-mv34dqsr-0163a6d9, which is stricter than my pattern and which I agree with). It compares in integer cents, 1..500, before any conversion, and toMicroUsd is no longer used for the ceiling.

The named NFR3 test (live-runner-refusal.test.js L62) refuses 37 values, which I counted from the source; the submission is right and the handoff's 38 is wrong. They include 5.0000001, 5.001, 4.999 and 1e0. It accepts 10 values, including 5, 5.00 and 0.50, and 6 refusals and 3 acceptances also go through a real process.

My probe (ev:ev-mv35auyr-010b9d52) passes 21 values the test does not list, all as expected: '4.995', '5.000', '5e-1', '٠.٥', '１', '5.0\r' and '000000000000005' refused; '3.33' accepted as 3330000. It also checks the order: the switch first, an empty value gives noCeiling, a bad ceiling is refused before the guard check, and a non-string is refused.

The pre-call print of provider, model, per-call cap, worst case, ceiling and `cli: claude 2.1.296` is asserted in the real-process test, which passes (ev:ev-mv34yg5i-0152378d).

RISK-21's possible spend is recorded as an upper bound of USD 1.10 (run.corrected on run-mv330tea-0177469c). Security confirms this with no residual.
